text:
## General Guidelines  
**Tone:** Professional, friendly, empathetic, patient  
**Key Points:**
- Always verify customer identity before discussing accounts
- Offer solutions, not excuses
- Know when to escalate (amounts >£1,000, complaints, fraud)
- Use document references ([[products]], [[policies]]) to answer product questions accurately
- Never promise what you can't deliver  
**Escalation Triggers:**
- Customer escalates to complaint
- Financial amount >£1,000
- Potential fraud
- Regulatory issue
- Customer very upset/angry

raw_entities.name: Customer Identity Verification Before Account Discussion
raw_entities.description: Staff must verify customer identity before discussing any account details or information. This is a foundational compliance requirement for all customer interactions.
context: Always verify customer identity before discussing accounts

raw_entities.name: Escalation for High-Value Transactions
raw_entities.description: Financial transactions or matters exceeding £1,000 must be escalated to a supervisor or appropriate authority. This threshold triggers mandatory escalation procedures.
context: Know when to escalate (amounts >£1,000, complaints, fraud)

raw_entities.name: Escalation for Customer Complaints
raw_entities.description: When a customer escalates an interaction to a formal complaint, staff must immediately escalate the matter through appropriate channels.
context: Know when to escalate (amounts >£1,000, complaints, fraud)
Customer escalates to complaint

raw_entities.name: Escalation for Potential Fraud
raw_entities.description: Any suspected or potential fraud must be immediately escalated to the fraud team or appropriate authority.
context: Know when to escalate (amounts >£1,000, complaints, fraud)
Potential fraud

raw_entities.name: Escalation for Regulatory Issues
raw_entities.description: Any matter involving potential regulatory breaches or compliance concerns must be escalated to the compliance or legal team.
context: Know when to escalate (amounts >£1,000, complaints, fraud)
Regulatory issue

raw_entities.name: Prohibition on Undeliverable Promises
raw_entities.description: Staff must never promise customers outcomes, solutions, or services that cannot be reliably delivered or guaranteed.
context: Never promise what you can't deliver

raw_entities.name: Use of Document References for Product Accuracy
raw_entities.description: When answering product questions, staff must reference authoritative product and policy documents to ensure accuracy and consistency.
context: Use document references ([[products]], [[policies]]) to answer product questions accurately

raw_entities.name: Customer Escalation to Formal Complaint
raw_entities.description: When a customer explicitly escalates an interaction to a formal complaint, this signals a breakdown in the initial resolution attempt and requires immediate escalation.
context: Customer escalates to complaint

raw_entities.name: Customer Extreme Emotional Distress
raw_entities.description: When a customer becomes very upset or angry, this is a warning sign that the interaction requires immediate de-escalation and escalation to a supervisor.
context: Customer very upset/angry
